findings.question: rc-tt-vm-0005
findings.quote: The footer naming the school health desk
findings.problem: The stem asks which element supplies a named contact, and this is the only choice that names an office. A reader can select it without reading the poster description, so the choice wording gives away the answer.
findings.fix: Use parallel choices naming poster elements only, such as the bottom banner, warning box, pie chart, and headline. Leave the contact information in the passage.

findings.question: q-text-types-visual-media-0019
findings.quote: The comic uses the sequence to connect a small exception with a shared problem. No caption blames one club alone; the crowded board reflects the combined actions of several students.
findings.problem: The passage explicitly supplies the interpretation of responsibility that this question asks readers to infer. The keyed choice, “Several small exceptions create a shared problem,” repeats that supplied conclusion, allowing readers to match wording instead of interpreting the panels.
findings.fix: Remove these interpretive sentences from the passage and retain the observable actions, dialogue, and expressions.

findings.question: rc-tt-vm-0001
findings.quote: stem: 'In the classroom example''s pie chart, which category has the largest share?
findings.problem: This stem uses a single-quoted multiline scalar instead of the block scalar (|) required by the style guide. The same formatting issue affects the stems and explanations of all 20 questions.
findings.fix: Convert all stem and explanation values to YAML block scalars (|), preserving their content and literal LaTeX backslashes.
